title: Split Into K Segments - Minimum Total Spread
source: Pattern reported by an Infosys SP candidate (Naukri Code360 experience, Jul 2024: hard DP problem splitting an array into K contiguous segments to minimise total segment cost). The cost function and constraints here are our own
statement:
You are given an array `A` of `N` integers and an integer `K`.

Split the array into **exactly `K` non-empty contiguous segments** (every element belongs to exactly one segment and the order is preserved).

The **spread** of a segment is `max(segment) − min(segment)`. Print the minimum possible sum of spreads over all `K` segments.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `N` and `K`.
The second line contains `N` space-separated integers `A[1..N]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum total spread.
hints: Focus on the **last** segment. If it is `A[j..i-1]`, the rest is the same problem on the prefix `A[0..j-1]` with one fewer segment.
`dp[s][i]` = minimum total spread splitting the first `i` elements into exactly `s` segments.
`dp[s][i] = min over j of dp[s-1][j] + spread(A[j..i-1])`. Iterate `j` from `i-1` **downwards** while maintaining the running max and min, so each spread costs `O(1)`.
editorial:
### State
`dp[s][i]` = minimum sum of spreads when the prefix `A[0..i-1]` (length `i`) is split into exactly `s` non-empty segments. Unreachable states are `∞`.

### Base case
`dp[1][i] = max(A[0..i-1]) − min(A[0..i-1])`.

### Transition
`dp[s][i] = min_{j = s-1 .. i-1} ( dp[s-1][j] + spread(A[j..i-1]) )`.
Walk `j` from `i-1` down to `s-1`, extending the last segment one element to the left and updating `hi`/`lo` - no extra precomputation needed.

### Order
Increasing `s`, and for each `s` any order of `i` (only row `s-1` is read) → two 1D arrays suffice.

### Answer
`dp[K][N]`.

### Complexity
`O(K · N^2 / 2)` ≈ `25 × 31 000 ≈ 8·10^5` steps.

### Common mistakes
- Allowing empty segments (start `j` at `s-1`, not `0`).
- Recomputing `max`/`min` of each slice from scratch (`O(K N^3)`).
- Assuming more segments always help and greedily cutting at the largest gaps - the segments must be contiguous in the **original** order, so sorting is not allowed.
